Boundaries of Welsh areas for maps

Source: R/boundaries.R
phw_boundaries.Rd

Downloads boundaries for one level of geography in Wales, from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) Open Geography Portal or DataMapWales, and returns them as an sf data frame ready for ggplot2::geom_sf(), with theme_phw_map(). Each download is saved in your user cache folder, so later calls work offline.

Usage

phw_boundaries(
  level,
  detail = c("generalised", "super", "ultra", "full"),
  crs = 27700,
  refresh = FALSE,
  cache = TRUE,
  quiet = FALSE
)

Arguments

level

The geography, e.g. "health_board", "local_authority", "gp_cluster", "lsoa". See phw_boundary_levels().

detail

How detailed the outlines are: "generalised" (20 m, the default and best for most maps), "super" (200 m), "ultra" (500 m, small files), or "full" (clipped to the coastline at full resolution). Where a level has no layer at that detail, the nearest one is used. DataMapWales layers come at full detail and are simplified with sf::st_simplify().

crs

Coordinate reference system of the result. Defaults to British National Grid (27700); use 4326 for longitude and latitude (e.g. for leaflet).

refresh

Download again even if a cached copy exists? If the download fails, the cached copy is used with a warning.

cache

Save the download in the cache folder?

quiet

Hide progress messages?

Value

An sf data frame with columns code, name and, where the source has one, name_cy (Welsh name), plus the geometry. Attributes source, layer and attribution say where it came from; use attr(x, "attribution") in your caption.

Details

See phw_boundary_levels() for the levels and the release used for each. The list of releases is updated in the package when new boundaries are published, so you get the newest boundaries by updating phwstyle and calling with refresh = TRUE.

Nothing is downloaded when phwstyle is installed. The first call for a level downloads it; later calls read the cached copy, so they are fast and work offline. Without an internet connection and without a cached copy, the function stops with an informative error. When a newer release of a level is downloaded, cached files from older releases of that level are deleted, so the cache stays small. Clear it all with phw_boundaries_cache(clear = TRUE).

Where a geography is published by more than one source, the others are tried in turn if the first cannot be reached, and a warning says which boundaries you were given. MSOAs and LSOAs come from DataMapWales, with the super generalised ONS boundaries as the alternative.

Publishers sometimes replace or withdraw a layer after a version of phwstyle is released. If none of the layers listed in your version can be downloaded, the function fetches the current list from the phwstyle repository on GitHub (a small text file, checked every week) and tries the layers in it, so an older installation keeps working. Set options(phwstyle.boundary_update = FALSE) to stop it looking. If that fails too and boundaries for the level were saved from an earlier release, those are returned with a warning.

See also

phw_boundary_levels(), phw_boundaries_cache()

Examples

phw_boundary_levels()
#>                       level                                          label
#> 1                   country                                Country (Wales)
#> 2              health_board                            Local health boards
#> 3           local_authority                              Local authorities
#> 4                gp_cluster                     GP (primary care) clusters
#> 5       senedd_constituency                          Senedd constituencies
#> 6  westminster_constituency                   UK Parliament constituencies
#> 7            electoral_ward                                Electoral wards
#> 8                 community Communities (community and town council areas)
#> 9                      msoa         Middle layer super output areas (2021)
#> 10                     lsoa          Lower layer super output areas (2021)
#> 11              output_area                            Output areas (2021)
#> 12              fire_rescue                    Fire and rescue authorities
#> 13             police_force                             Police force areas
#>          source release                          detail
#> 1           ons    2025 full, generalised, super, ultra
#> 2           ons    2023        full, generalised, ultra
#> 3           ons    2026 full, generalised, super, ultra
#> 4  datamapwales    2024                            full
#> 5           ons    2026        full, generalised, super
#> 6           ons    2024 full, generalised, super, ultra
#> 7           ons    2026        full, generalised, super
#> 8  datamapwales    2022                            full
#> 9  datamapwales    2021                     full, super
#> 10 datamapwales    2021                     full, super
#> 11          ons    2021                     generalised
#> 12          ons    2024        full, generalised, ultra
#> 13          ons    2024        full, generalised, ultra
# \donttest{
if (requireNamespace("sf", quietly = TRUE) && interactive()) {
  hb <- phw_boundaries("health_board")
  library(ggplot2)
  ggplot(hb) +
    geom_sf(aes(fill = name)) +
    scale_fill_phw_d() +
    theme_phw_map() +
    labs(caption = attr(hb, "attribution"))
}
# }
